value.name: confirms Devin's signature
value.description: Asha checks the page closely and confirms that Devin's signature has been cleanly set on the line.
evidence: lifted it close enough to confirm Devin's signature had set clean on the line.

value.name: receives Rosa's supportive text
value.description: Asha's phone buzzes with a text from Rosa telling her she can say whatever she needs to Whitfield and that Devin signed in good faith because she was absent.
evidence: Her phone buzzed on the laminate while she was checking the ink, and Rosa's text was two sentences long: that whatever Asha needed to say to Whitfield was hers to say, and that the boy had signed in good faith because Asha had not been there, which was a thing Whitfield ought to hear in full.

value.name: chooses not to reply
value.description: Asha reads Rosa's message twice and deliberately does not answer.
evidence: Asha read it twice and did not answer.

value.name: secures the page in her case
value.description: Asha slides the signed page into the inner sleeve of her case, takes her coat, and heads toward the elevator.
evidence: She slid the page into the inner sleeve of her case, took her coat from the back of the chair, and walked out toward the elevator with the paper gripped at the corner the way she carried filings to court,

value.name: feels the hallway lengthen
value.description: As Asha leaves, the hallway feels unusually long to her, underscoring her tension before the confrontation ahead.
evidence: although the hallway felt longer than it had on any other Monday she could remember.

value.name: steadies herself in the elevator
value.description: In the elevator, Asha closes her eyes, tightens her grip on the case, and feels the page against her palm while Rosa texts again.
evidence: In the elevator Asha closed her eyes for the length of a breath and tightened her grip on the leather case, feeling the corner of the page through the lining against her palm.
Her phone buzzed before the doors finished closing: Rosa again, two lines this time, that the boy signed because Asha had not been there, and that Whitfield ought to hear it that way.

value.name: refuses to answer in the elevator
value.description: Asha reads Rosa's second message and lets the screen go dark, deciding not to respond until she is in front of Whitfield.
evidence: She read it once and let the screen go dark without answering, because answering would mean choosing the sentence now, in the elevator, and she had told herself she would choose it standing in front of his desk.

value.name: rides up toward Whitfield's floor
value.description: Asha experiences the case as heavier on the way up and arrives on the partners' floor composed enough to step out steadily.
evidence: the case felt heavier on the way up than it had in the hallway, which she registered as a fact about her arm and not about the paper, and when the doors opened on the partners' floor she walked out steady,
